intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt from Reykjavik
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour departing from central Reykjavik to chase the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the clearest skies, often heading toward the Reykjanes Peninsula or Þingvellir area. Includes hot chocolate and photography tips.
experiences.location: Departing from Reykjavik City Centre, Capital Region

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters of the Blue Lagoon, located just 20 minutes from Reykjavik and conveniently near Keflavik Airport. Enjoy silica mud masks, swim-up bars, and steam caves. Book the Comfort package for access to towels and a drink included in the entry.

experiences.name: Golden Circle Day Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's most celebrated natural route covering Þingvellir National Park (a UNESCO World Heritage Site where tectonic plates meet), the erupting Strokkur geyser at Geysir, and the thundering Gullfoss waterfall. Easily accessible from Reykjavik, making it ideal for centrally located travellers.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water at Silfra, located within Þingvellir National Park — the same area as the Golden Circle. Visibility exceeds 100 metres in some of the world's purest water. Dry suits are provided. Combine with the Golden Circle for a full day.

experiences.name: Laugardalslaug Geothermal Pool & Local Food at Hlemmur Mathöll
experiences.description: Start your morning with a soak at Laugardalslaug, Reykjavik's largest public geothermal pool complex featuring hot pots, steam rooms, and a waterslide — a true local experience just 2 km from the city centre. Afterward, head to Hlemmur Mathöll food hall for an authentic Icelandic lunch featuring lamb soup, skyr desserts, and fresh seafood from local vendors.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or a budget shuttle to Reykjavik BSI terminal, then arrange onward travel north toward Siglufjörður. The drive is approximately 4-5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel. Rest and recover from the flight during the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in early if possible at Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10, or store luggage and take a gentle walk along the harbour front to get oriented. Siglufjörður is a charming small fishing town nestled in a dramatic fjord — explore the colourful wooden houses and the quiet harbour area.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the hotel and rest after the long travel day. As darkness falls (which comes early in January), step outside or find a dark spot near the harbour to watch for the Northern Lights — January skies in northern Iceland offer excellent aurora opportunities. Dress in all your warmest layers.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at Keflavik Airport before departure — budget around 1,000–1,500 ISK for a pastry and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or snacks from a Reykjavik Bonus or Krónan supermarket before heading north to save money on the road.
meals.dinner: Visit Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður for a local meal — try the fish soup, a hearty and affordable Icelandic staple (around 2,500–3,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: January days in Siglufjörður are very short — expect only 4–5 hours of daylight. The road north can be icy and subject to closures; check road.is before driving. Consider renting a 4WD vehicle for safety. Budget tip: buy groceries at a Reykjavik supermarket (Bonus or Krónan) before leaving the capital as prices are significantly lower than in small towns.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's most acclaimed regional museums, documenting the herring fishing boom of the early 20th century. Entry is around 2,000 ISK and well worth it. Explore the beautifully restored harbour buildings and exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or walk to the nearby Hofsós village (approximately 45 minutes south along Route 76) to see the stunning infinity geothermal pool perched above the fjord. The Hofsós Swimming Pool offers incredible views of Skagafjörður and costs only around 1,000–1,200 ISK to enter — a true budget hot spring gem.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark. As evening falls, head to a high point above the town — the hillside above the harbour is ideal — and scan the sky for Northern Lights. The low light pollution in this remote fjord makes it one of the best aurora-viewing spots in Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at the hotel using groceries purchased in Reykjavik — bread, skyr, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of soup and sandwiches from the hotel kitchen or local grocery store for the Hofsós trip.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the hotel if kitchen facilities are available, or visit the local Við Árbakkann café in Siglufjörður for a budget-friendly bowl of lamb soup (kjötsúpa) for around 2,000–2,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós pool may have limited winter hours — call ahead or check online before visiting. Road conditions on Route 76 can be challenging in January; always check road.is. Bring a swimsuit and towel for the pool.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the scenic Skagafjörður valley (approximately 1 hour) to explore the historic Glaumbær turf farm museum. This beautifully preserved 18th-century turf farmstead offers a fascinating glimpse into traditional Icelandic rural life. Entry is around 1,800 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the town of Varmahlíð and visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum for more regional history. Alternatively, take a short hike along the Héraðsvatn river valley — the landscape is dramatic even in winter. Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal road.
day_by_day.evening: Aurora hunting evening — drive a short distance out of Siglufjörður toward the Héðinsfjörður tunnel entrance and park in a dark area away from town lights. Bring a tripod if you have one for aurora photography. The clear, dark skies of the northern fjords are ideal.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel — skyr with granola, toast, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Stop at Café Á Brekku in Varmahlíð for a light lunch — soup and bread for around 1,800–2,200 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hotel — pasta with canned fish or a simple stew using ingredients from the local Samkaup store in Siglufjörður.

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær museum may have reduced winter hours or be closed — verify before visiting at glaumbaer.is. The drive back to Siglufjörður in the dark requires caution on icy roads. Always carry an emergency kit, warm blankets, and a charged phone when driving in Iceland in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Siglufjörður on foot — walk the full length of the harbour and up into the residential streets to admire the colourful wooden architecture. Visit the small local church (Siglufjörðarkirkja) and the town's memorial to herring workers. The town is compact and very walkable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive through the dramatic Héðinsfjörður tunnel (opened 2010) to the neighbouring fjord of Ólafsfjörður — a 20-minute drive. Walk around this equally charming small fishing village and visit the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Ólafsfjarðar) for a warm soak — entry around 1,000 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður and enjoy a relaxed evening. Check the aurora forecast on vedur.is — if cloud cover is low and the KP index is favourable, head out for aurora viewing along the fjord shore. The reflections of the Northern Lights on the still fjord waters can be spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Pick up a hot dog (pylsa) from a local petrol station or small shop — Iceland's iconic budget snack at around 500–700 ISK.
meals.dinner: Visit Hannes Boy in Siglufjörður for their fish of the day — fresh Arctic char or cod is typically available and affordable at around 3,000–4,000 ISK for a main course.

day_by_day.notes: The Héðinsfjörður tunnel is toll-free. Ólafsfjörður is a very small town with limited services — the swimming pool is the main attraction. January swimming pools in Iceland are wonderfully warm and uncrowded.

day_by_day.morning: Take a winter nature walk in the mountains above Siglufjörður. The valley behind the town offers accessible trails even in winter — follow the marked path toward Hólsfjall for panoramic views of the fjord below. Dress in full winter gear including crampons or microspikes for icy paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Museum annex buildings — the Boat House and the Saltfish House — which are part of the Herring Era Museum complex. Spend time learning about the maritime heritage of the region. Alternatively, relax at the local Siglufjörður Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — entry around 1,000 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local community event if available (check with the hotel for any winter cultural events). Otherwise, enjoy a cosy evening in the hotel with a book, and step outside periodically to check for Northern Lights — set an aurora alert on the Vedur app.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel — eggs, toast, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Self-catered packed lunch for the mountain walk — sandwiches, chocolate, and a thermos of hot tea.
meals.dinner: Cook a budget meal at the hotel — Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa) using lamb from the local Samkaup store, which is both affordable and warming.

day_by_day.notes: Mountain walks in January require careful preparation — check weather forecasts on vedur.is before heading out. Never hike alone in winter conditions. Inform the hotel of your plans. The Siglufjörður swimming pool is a great social hub where you can meet locals.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east along Route 76 toward Dalvík (approximately 1.5 hours). Stop at the scenic viewpoints along the coastal road overlooking Eyjafjörður — Iceland's longest fjord. The winter landscape of snow-capped mountains reflected in the dark fjord waters is breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Dalvík and visit the Hvoll Museum, which houses a fascinating exhibit on the largest man ever born in Iceland. Walk along the Dalvík harbour and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere of this small fishing community. Visit the Dalvík Swimming Pool for a warm soak — entry around 1,000 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður along the coast, timing the return for the best chance of aurora viewing. The stretch of road between Dalvík and Ólafsfjörður, away from town lights, is an excellent aurora-watching spot. Pull over safely if the lights appear.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Visit Gísli, Eiríkur, Helgi restaurant in Dalvík — a beloved local spot known for affordable fish dishes and lamb soup (around 2,000–3,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hotel upon return — pasta, canned fish, or leftovers.

day_by_day.notes: The coastal road between Siglufjörður and Dalvík is scenic but can be icy and narrow in places. Allow extra travel time in winter. Dalvík is also the departure point for whale watching tours, though these are limited in January.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Akureyri — Iceland's second-largest city, approximately 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður via Route 82 and Route 1. Arrive and explore the charming town centre on foot. Visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill above the town — free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's most northerly botanical garden, free to enter. Even in January the grounds are atmospheric in the snow. Browse the shops along Hafnarstræti, the main pedestrian street. Visit the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) for a budget-friendly cultural experience (around 1,500 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Soak at the Akureyri Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — one of Iceland's best public pools with hot tubs and steam rooms, entry around 1,100 ISK. Drive back to Siglufjörður in the evening, watching for Northern Lights on the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Visit Bláa Kannan café in Akureyri for soup and bread — a cosy and affordable option at around 1,800–2,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Try Strikið restaurant in Akureyri for their budget lunch/early dinner menu, or grab a burger from Hamborgarabúlla Tómasar for around 2,000–2,500 ISK before heading back.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a significant town with supermarkets (Bonus, Krónan) — stock up on groceries here for the coming days as prices are lower than in Siglufjörður. The drive back in the dark requires care; the road via Öxnadalur can be particularly icy.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the hotel. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Use the morning to plan the remaining days, charge devices, do laundry, and review the aurora forecast for the coming nights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate surroundings of Siglufjörður more deeply — walk along the fjord shore toward the end of the valley. The dramatic mountain walls rising directly from the water are stunning in winter light. Look for Arctic birds along the shoreline including eider ducks and purple sandpipers.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated Northern Lights evening — drive to the Héðinsfjörður area (the old abandoned fjord accessible via a short tunnel) for completely dark skies and dramatic mountain scenery. Bring hot drinks in a thermos, warm blankets, and a camera on a tripod. Stay out for 2–3 hours if conditions are favourable.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely self-catered breakfast — eggs, toast, skyr, coffee.
meals.lunch: Self-catered lunch at the hotel using Akureyri groceries.
meals.dinner: Cook a proper meal at the hotel — Icelandic lamb chops or pan-fried cod with potatoes and vegetables, using fresh ingredients from Akureyri.

day_by_day.notes: Héðinsfjörður is an abandoned fjord with no permanent residents — it is completely dark at night, making it ideal for aurora photography. The road into the fjord (beyond the tunnel) may be impassable in winter; check conditions. The tunnel itself is a good stopping point.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south to explore the Skagafjörður region more thoroughly. Visit the historic Hólar í Hjaltadal — Iceland's ancient ecclesiastical centre and former bishopric. The cathedral and surrounding historic buildings are fascinating, and the setting in the valley is beautiful. Free to explore the grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Reykjafoss and Kolufoss waterfalls in the Víðidalur valley — dramatic winter waterfalls partially frozen in ice. The drive through the valley is scenic and the waterfalls are accessible with care. Return via Varmahlíð.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Stop at the Samkaup store for any needed supplies. Enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel with aurora monitoring — set the Vedur app to alert you if the KP index rises above 3.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos and sandwiches for the day trip — eat at the Hólar cathedral grounds.
meals.dinner: Visit Við Árbakkann café in Siglufjörður for a warming dinner — fish soup and bread for around 2,000–2,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Hólar has a small university and agricultural college — the campus is active even in winter. The road to Kolufoss may require a 4WD vehicle in January. Always check road.is before venturing onto secondary roads.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Siglufjörður along the northern coast toward Húsavík (approximately 2.5 hours via Route 85). This is a longer day trip but highly rewarding. The coastal scenery along the way is dramatic with sea cliffs and frozen waterfalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Húsavík — the whale watching capital of Iceland. Visit the Húsavík Whale Museum (Hvalasafnið) for an excellent and affordable introduction to Iceland's whale species — entry around 2,000 ISK. Walk along the charming harbour and visit the iconic wooden church.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive to Siglufjörður, stopping at dark spots along the way for aurora viewing. The remote stretch of Route 85 between Húsavík and Akureyri offers excellent dark sky conditions. Aim to be back in Siglufjörður by 22:00.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Visit Gamli Baukur restaurant in Húsavík for their famous fish soup — a local institution at around 2,500 ISK for soup and bread.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hotel upon return — keep it simple with pasta or soup after a long driving day.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — approximately 5 hours total. Ensure the vehicle is fuelled up before leaving Siglufjörður as petrol stations are sparse on this route. The road via Grenivík and along the eastern shore of Eyjafjörður is particularly scenic.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning in Siglufjörður. Visit the local swimming pool for a morning soak and to socialise with locals — a quintessential Icelandic experience. The hot pots (heitir pottar) are perfect for warming up on a cold January morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a guided or self-guided walk through the old herring processing district of Siglufjörður — the restored factory buildings along the harbour are atmospheric in winter. Visit the Segull 67 craft brewery (if open) for a locally brewed beer tasting — a small tasting flight costs around 1,500–2,000 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Final dedicated aurora hunting night — this is statistically one of the best times of year for Northern Lights viewing in northern Iceland. Drive to the highest accessible point above Siglufjörður for a 360-degree view. Bring all warm clothing, hot drinks, and a camera. Stay out as long as conditions allow.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel — skyr, bread, and fruit.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly more indulgent dinner at Hannes Boy — try the Arctic char with local vegetables for around 4,000–5,000 ISK as a special occasion meal.

day_by_day.notes: Segull 67 brewery has limited opening hours — check their Facebook page before visiting. The aurora forecast for this evening should be checked on vedur.is and spaceweather.com. January 2027 falls during an active period of Solar Cycle 25, which should provide excellent aurora activity.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day in the Siglufjörður area. Take a slow morning walk along the entire length of the fjord shore, from the harbour to the valley end. Photograph the town in the soft winter light — the golden hour lasts most of the morning in January at this latitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back to Akureyri (1.5 hours) for a final afternoon of exploration. Visit the Akureyri Museum (Minjasafnið á Akureyri) for local history — entry around 1,500 ISK. Stock up on any Icelandic souvenirs at the Bonus supermarket (much cheaper than tourist shops) — Icelandic chocolate, dried fish, and skyr are great budget gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a final evening. Pack bags for the next day's departure. Enjoy a farewell dinner and one last aurora watch from the harbour. Reflect on the incredible landscapes, hot springs, and natural wonders experienced over the past 12 days.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel — use up remaining groceries.
meals.lunch: Visit Bláa Kannan in Akureyri for a final café lunch — soup, sandwich, and coffee for around 2,000–2,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Final dinner at Við Árbakkann or Hannes Boy in Siglufjörður — order the fish of the day and a bowl of skyr for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Pack carefully tonight and set an early alarm for tomorrow. Confirm the return journey route to Keflavik and check road conditions on road.is. If flying from Akureyri domestic airport, the journey is much shorter — check if your return flight departs from Akureyri or Keflavik.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Siglufjörður. The drive to Keflavik International Airport takes approximately 5–6 hours depending on road conditions. Depart by 06:00 at the latest for an afternoon or evening flight. Stop in Akureyri if needed for fuel and a final coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive south via Route 1 through the Hvalfjörður tunnel or over the mountain pass toward Reykjavik and Keflavik. If time allows before the flight, stop at the Blue Lagoon (Bláa Lónið) near Keflavik for a final hot spring soak — book in advance as it sells out; entry starts at around 9,990 ISK for the Comfort package.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport. Check in, clear security, and browse the duty-free shops. Reflect on an incredible 13-day budget adventure through northern Iceland — from the aurora-lit skies of Siglufjörður to the geothermal pools of Hofsós and the whale museum of Húsavík.

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast at the hotel before departure — use up all remaining food.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks for the road to avoid expensive motorway stops.
meals.dinner: Eat at Keflavik Airport — budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK for a meal at one of the airport restaurants, or bring food from Reykjavik if stopping there.

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra travel time in January due to potential road closures, ice, and reduced visibility. The Hvalfjörður tunnel costs around 1,500 ISK toll but saves significant time compared to driving around the fjord. Return the rental car with a full tank of petrol — refuel before reaching the airport as airport fuel is more expensive. Budget summary: accommodation at Hotel Siglunes, car rental, fuel, pool entries, museum entries, and meals should total approximately 180,000–220,000 ISK (€1,200–€1,500) for the 13 days if managed carefully.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or rent a car toward Reykjavik. Check into a transit guesthouse or use luggage storage to freshen up. Given the very early arrival and long drive north ahead, spend the morning resting and exploring central Reykjavik on foot — stroll around Hallgrímskirkja church and the old harbour area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (pre-booked, located 20 minutes from the airport — ideal to stop en route before heading north). Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters, enjoy the steam rooms and silica mud masks. This is a perfect way to recover from the overnight flight. Depart by 15:00 and begin the scenic drive north toward Siglufjörður (approximately 5–6 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel).
day_by_day.afternoon_note: Drive north through Borgarnes and Varmahlíð, stopping briefly at a petrol station for snacks. Roads may be icy — drive cautiously.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður by approximately 21:00–22:00. Check in, unpack, and settle into this charming fishing village hotel. Step outside briefly to scan the sky for the northern lights — Siglufjörður's remote location and minimal light pollution make it an excellent aurora-viewing spot.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at a café near Keflavik Airport or the Flybus terminal (e.g., Kaffitár) — budget around 1,500–2,000 ISK.
meals.lunch: Stop at Bjarteyjarsandur farm café or a petrol station diner along Route 1 near Borgarnes for a hearty bowl of lamb soup — budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dine at Hotel Siglunes's own restaurant or the nearby Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður, known for fresh fish and local lamb dishes — budget around 4,000–6,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Blue Lagoon well in advance as slots sell out. Rent a 4WD vehicle for safety on northern Icelandic winter roads. Download the Veður app (Icelandic Met Office) and 112.is emergency app before departure. Carry warm layers, as temperatures will be around 0–5°C.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, wake up and explore Siglufjörður village on foot. Visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), which tells the fascinating story of Iceland's herring boom in the early 20th century. The museum is one of Iceland's best regional museums and is a short walk from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Tröllaskagi Peninsula route (Route 82) south toward Hofsós, stopping at viewpoints overlooking the dramatic fjords and snow-dusted mountains. Visit the Hofsós Infinity Pool — a stunning geothermal swimming pool perched on a cliff edge overlooking Skagafjörður fjord. Swim in the warm geothermal water with panoramic winter views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður by late afternoon. As darkness falls early (sunset around 15:30 in January), position yourself on the hillside above town or the harbour for northern lights watching. The clear fjord skies and surrounding mountains create a dramatic aurora backdrop. Check aurora forecast on vedur.is.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy the hotel breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — typically includes skyr, bread, eggs, and coffee — usually included or around 2,000–2,500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch from a local grocery store (Krónan or Nettó) — pick up skyr, rye bread, smoked salmon, and fruit — budget around 1,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dine at Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður for fresh Arctic char or pan-fried cod with local vegetables — budget around 4,500–6,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós Pool is open year-round but check winter hours (typically 07:00–21:00). Bring a swimsuit and towel. The drive to Hofsós is approximately 45 minutes each way on Route 76/82 — roads may be snowy, so drive carefully. Aurora activity is best after 21:00 on clear nights.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður toward Akureyri (approximately 1.5 hours via the Héðinsfjörður tunnel and Route 82). Arrive in Akureyri, Iceland's second-largest city. Explore the charming town centre — visit Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill, browse the botanical garden (Lystigarðurinn), and walk along Hafnarstræti, the main shopping street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Akureyri's geothermal swimming pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — a large public pool complex with hot tubs, steam rooms, and a waterslide, beloved by locals. Spend 1–2 hours soaking and relaxing. Afterward, explore the Akureyri Art Museum or the Nonni House museum dedicated to children's author Jón Sveinsson.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Akureyri's modest but vibrant dining scene for dinner. Return to Siglufjörður by 21:00 (1.5-hour drive). On the return journey, pull over at a dark spot along Route 82 to watch for the northern lights over the fjords.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Siglunes before departing.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Rub23 in Akureyri — a popular mid-range restaurant known for fresh sushi and grilled fish — budget around 3,500–5,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dine at Strikið restaurant in Akureyri before heading back — known for Icelandic lamb and seafood with fjord views — budget around 5,000–7,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a great base for day trips. Parking is free in the town centre on weekends and evenings. The geothermal pool costs approximately 1,000–1,200 ISK entry. Bring a swimsuit. Check road conditions on road.is before driving.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Lake Mývatn, approximately 1 hour east of Akureyri on Route 1. Begin with the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a less-crowded alternative to the Blue Lagoon with stunning volcanic landscape views. Soak in the silica-rich geothermal water surrounded by lava fields and steam vents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mývatn volcanic landscape: walk among the eerie Dimmuborgir lava formations (often called the 'Dark Castles'), visit the Skútustaðagígar pseudocraters (a UNESCO-protected area), and hike up Hverfjall crater rim for panoramic views of the lake and surrounding lava fields. The crater hike takes approximately 1 hour.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Siglufjörður via Akureyri. Stop at Goðafoss waterfall ('Waterfall of the Gods') on Route 1 — beautifully lit by car headlights and moonlight in winter. Arrive back at the hotel by 21:00. Check aurora forecast and step outside for northern lights viewing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Siglunes before departing.
meals.lunch: Café at Mývatn Nature Baths or Vogafjós Farm Resort near Mývatn — try the geothermal rye bread (hverabrauð) baked underground, served with smoked trout — budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Pick up groceries in Akureyri on the way back (Bónus supermarket) and prepare a simple meal at the hotel, or dine at a local Akureyri spot like Greifinn for pizza and pasta — budget around 3,000–4,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths entry is approximately 6,500 ISK per person — book online in advance. Dress in waterproof layers as wind can be strong near the lake. Goðafoss is accessible year-round and free to visit. Total driving for the day is approximately 3.5–4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning in Siglufjörður. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Take a slow morning walk along the harbour and the old fish factory ruins. Visit the Folk Music Centre (Tónlistarsafnið) in Siglufjörður, which celebrates Iceland's rich tradition of folk music and the Íslenski þátturinn (Icelandic tune).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Sauðárkrókur (approximately 1 hour south on Route 76), the largest town in Skagafjörður. Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum and explore the town. Stop at the Glaumbær turf farm museum on the way — one of Iceland's best-preserved historic turf farmsteads, offering a fascinating glimpse into 18th–19th century Icelandic rural life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner at the hotel. Spend the evening on a self-guided northern lights hunt — drive a few kilometres out of town along Route 76 to escape any ambient light and watch the sky. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate and a blanket.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Siglunes.
meals.lunch: Café Ólafs in Sauðárkrókur or a local bakery — try a bowl of kjötsúpa (Icelandic lamb soup) and fresh bread — budget around 2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes restaurant — try the pan-seared Arctic char with root vegetables — budget around 4,500–6,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær turf farm may have limited winter hours — check ahead (typically open 10:00–16:00 in winter). Entry is approximately 1,800 ISK. This is a lighter activity day to allow for rest mid-trip. Aurora forecast: check vedur.is each evening.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 3.5–4 hours via Route 1 and Route 54). This is a longer travel day. Stop at Borgarnes Settlement Centre on the way — an excellent interactive museum about the Viking Age settlement of Iceland, based on the Egils Saga.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula and explore Snæfellsjökull National Park. Visit Arnarstapi and Hellnar coastal villages with their dramatic basalt sea cliffs and lava arches. Walk the 2.5 km coastal path between the two villages — one of Iceland's most scenic short hikes, with crashing waves and bird colonies (even in winter).
day_by_day.evening: Check into a guesthouse near Grundarfjörður or Stykkishólmur for the night (pre-booked mid-range accommodation). Visit Kirkjufell mountain — the iconic 'arrowhead' peak — at dusk and after dark for northern lights photography with the mountain as a foreground. This is one of Iceland's most photographed aurora locations.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Siglunes before departing.
meals.lunch: Stop at a petrol station café in Borgarnes or grab a meal at the Settlement Centre café — budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dine at Bjargarsteinn Mathús in Arnarstapi or Grundarfjörður Guesthouse restaurant — fresh fish and lamb dishes — budget around 4,500–6,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest driving day of the trip (~4 hours). Start early. Book Snæfellsnes accommodation well in advance as options are limited in winter. Kirkjufell is best photographed with a tripod — bring one if interested in aurora photography. Roads on the peninsula can be icy.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Snæfellsjökull glacier and national park. Drive up toward the glacier base (road conditions permitting) and walk among the lava fields at Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach — a hauntingly beautiful volcanic beach with rusted shipwreck remains and lifting stones used by fishermen to test strength. Visit Lóndrangar basalt sea stacks nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Stykkishólmur, the charming main town of the peninsula. Visit the Norwegian House (Norska Húsið) museum and climb the Súgandisey lighthouse island for panoramic views over the Breiðafjörður bay and its thousands of islands. Browse the local shops and the harbour.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back toward Reykjavik (approximately 2 hours from Stykkishólmur). Check into a mid-range hotel or guesthouse in Reykjavik for the next several nights (e.g., Guesthouse Butterfly or similar). Explore the Laugavegur street area in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Snæfellsnes guesthouse.
meals.lunch: Narfeyrarstofa restaurant in Stykkishólmur — famous for fresh mussels from Breiðafjörður bay — budget around 3,500–5,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dine in Reykjavik at Matur og Drykkur — a celebrated restaurant serving traditional Icelandic recipes with a modern twist — budget around 5,500–8,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Djúpalónssandur beach has four lifting stones — try the 'Fullsterkur' (full strength) stone at 154 kg! The beach is free to visit. Stykkishólmur is a lovely town worth 2–3 hours of exploration. Confirm Reykjavik hotel check-in time before arriving.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a soak at Laugardalslaug, Reykjavik's largest public geothermal pool complex. Swim laps in the outdoor heated pool, relax in the hot tubs (ranging from 38–44°C), and enjoy the steam room. This is where locals come to socialise and unwind — a truly authentic Reykjavik experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavik's cultural highlights: visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) for a comprehensive overview of Icelandic history from settlement to modern times. Walk through the colourful old town (Vesturbær), visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Hafnarhús), and stroll along the Sæbraut coastal path.
day_by_day.evening: Join a Northern Lights Hunt guided minibus tour departing from central Reykjavik. Expert guides use real-time aurora forecasts and cloud cover maps to drive to the best viewing locations outside the city. Tours typically run 21:00–01:00 and include aurora photography tips.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Hlemmur Mathöll food hall — try skyr with granola and a flat white from one of the vendors — budget around 1,800–2,500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hlemmur Mathöll — explore the various stalls offering everything from Icelandic fish tacos to lamb sandwiches — budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Pre-tour dinner at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic food including hákarl (fermented shark), rye bread ice cream, and lamb stew — budget around 3,500–5,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Laugardalslaug entry is approximately 1,100 ISK. Bring a swimsuit and towel (or rent on-site for ~500 ISK). Northern Lights tour costs approximately 9,000–12,000 ISK per person — book in advance. Tours are weather-dependent and reputable operators offer free rebooking if aurora is not visible.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Golden Circle Day Tour — Iceland's most celebrated natural route. Begin at Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site), where you can walk in the rift valley between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Visit the Öxará river and the historic Alþingi parliament site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 metres into the air. Then visit Gullfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful and dramatic waterfalls, partially frozen in January with ice formations along the canyon walls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the city. If energy allows, take a second attempt at northern lights viewing from Öskjuhlíð hill (Perlan area) on the edge of Reykjavik — a good city-accessible aurora spot.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Geysir Center café near Strokkur — lamb soup and fresh bread — budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) in Reykjavik — Icelandic steakhouse with locally sourced lamb and fish — budget around 6,000–8,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle can be done independently by rental car (approximately 300 km round trip) or on a guided tour (approximately 8,000–12,000 ISK). Self-driving allows more flexibility. Þingvellir and Gullfoss are free to visit. Dress in waterproof layers — Gullfoss spray can be intense even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavik). Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 metres. The water temperature is 2–4°C year-round — dry suits are provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Silfra experience, warm up with hot chocolate and explore the Þingvellir visitor centre. Drive back toward Reykjavik and stop at the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool in a rustic outdoor setting, much less crowded than the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Explore the Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur streets for souvenir shopping and gallery browsing. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range Reykjavik restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before the early departure for Silfra (tours typically start 08:00–09:00).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks provided by the tour operator, or stop at a café in Selfoss on the way to the Secret Lagoon — budget around 2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) in Reykjavik harbour — famous for lobster soup and grilled fish skewers — budget around 3,000–4,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling tours cost approximately 18,000–22,000 ISK per person — book well in advance as spots are limited. Minimum age is typically 12 years. No prior diving experience needed for snorkeling. The Secret Lagoon entry is approximately 3,000 ISK. Bring a swimsuit and towel.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip along the South Coast of Iceland. Drive east on Route 1 to Seljalandsfoss waterfall — a stunning 60-metre cascade that you can walk behind (path may be icy/closed in January — check conditions). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall, one of Iceland's largest and most dramatic falls, with a staircase to the top for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — one of the world's most dramatic beaches, with towering basalt columns (Reynisdrangar sea stacks), powerful Atlantic waves, and black volcanic sand. Walk along the beach but stay well back from the waves (sneaker waves are dangerous). Visit the Dyrhólaey promontory for coastal views.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Reykjavik (approximately 2.5 hours). Stop at a petrol station for a hot drink. Arrive back by 20:00–21:00. Enjoy a final evening in Reykjavik with dinner and a walk along the illuminated harbour.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Skógarfoss Café or the Vík í Mýrdal village — try fish and chips or lamb burger — budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Fiskmarkaðurinn (The Fish Market) in Reykjavik — creative Icelandic seafood with Asian influences — budget around 6,000–8,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast drive is approximately 500 km round trip — a full day. Start by 08:00. Reynisfjara beach is extremely dangerous — never turn your back on the ocean. Seljalandsfoss walk-behind path is often closed in winter due to ice — check ahead. Bring microspikes/crampons for icy paths.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed final full day in Reykjavik. Visit the Perlan Museum — a stunning glass dome building with a 360° observation deck offering panoramic views over Reykjavik and the surrounding mountains. Inside, explore the excellent 'Wonders of Iceland' exhibition with a real ice cave tunnel, northern lights planetarium show, and glacier exhibit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjavik Botanical Garden (Grasagarðurinn) in Laugardalur for a peaceful winter walk. Browse the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) for vintage Icelandic woolens, second-hand books, and local food stalls. Alternatively, visit the Árbær Open Air Museum for a glimpse of historic Reykjavik buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner at one of Reykjavik's best mid-range restaurants. Take a final northern lights attempt — either join a last-minute tour or drive to Grótta lighthouse on the Seltjarnarnes peninsula (15 minutes from central Reykjavik) for a dark sky spot with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to breakfast at Brauð & Co bakery — famous for their cinnamon rolls and sourdough — budget around 1,500–2,000 ISK.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Messinn restaurant — known for their cast-iron pan-fried fish of the day — budget around 3,500–5,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Apotek Kitchen & Bar in central Reykjavik — elegant but accessible, serving Icelandic lamb, seafood, and creative cocktails — budget around 6,000–9,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Perlan Museum entry is approximately 4,990 ISK — book online for a small discount. The northern lights planetarium show inside Perlan is a great backup if the real aurora is not visible. Grótta lighthouse is free and accessible by car — check tide times as the path can flood at high tide.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Pack and check out. If your flight is in the afternoon or evening, store luggage at the hotel or at BSÍ bus terminal. Take a final walk along Tjörnin lake in central Reykjavik — often partially frozen in January with ducks and swans — and visit the City Hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, stop at the Blue Lagoon again on the way to the airport (pre-book a short 2-hour slot) for a final geothermal soak, or browse duty-free shops at Keflavik Airport. Pick up Icelandic chocolate, skyr snacks, and lopapeysa (traditional Icelandic wool sweaters) as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Keflavik International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of northern lights, geothermal pools, dramatic landscapes, and Icelandic culture.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast in Reykjavik.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near Tjörnin lake (e.g., Café Paris or Kaffitár) — soup and sandwich — budget around 2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the airport or Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant if stopping there — budget around 4,000–6,000 ISK, or grab a meal deal at the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the drive to Keflavik (45 minutes from Reykjavik) plus check-in and security. Return your rental car with a full tank — petrol stations near the airport include N1 and Orkan. The Blue Lagoon is 20 minutes from the airport — a perfect final stop if time allows.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt from Reykjavik
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour departing from central Reykjavik to chase the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the clearest skies, often heading toward the Reykjanes Peninsula or Þingvellir area. Includes hot chocolate and photography tips.
experiences.location: Departing from Reykjavik City Centre, Capital Region

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters of the Blue Lagoon, located just 20 minutes from Reykjavik and conveniently near Keflavik Airport. Enjoy silica mud masks, swim-up bars, and steam caves. Book the Comfort package for access to towels and a drink included in the entry.

experiences.name: Golden Circle Day Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's most celebrated natural route covering Þingvellir National Park (a UNESCO World Heritage Site where tectonic plates meet), the erupting Strokkur geyser at Geysir, and the thundering Gullfoss waterfall. Easily accessible from Reykjavik, making it ideal for centrally located travellers.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water at Silfra, located within Þingvellir National Park — the same area as the Golden Circle. Visibility exceeds 100 metres in some of the world's purest water. Dry suits are provided. Combine with the Golden Circle for a full day.

experiences.name: Laugardalslaug Geothermal Pool & Local Food at Hlemmur Mathöll
experiences.description: Start your morning with a soak at Laugardalslaug, Reykjavik's largest public geothermal pool complex featuring hot pots, steam rooms, and a waterslide — a true local experience just 2 km from the city centre. Afterward, head to Hlemmur Mathöll food hall for an authentic Icelandic lunch featuring lamb soup, skyr desserts, and fresh seafood from local vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Transfer to Reykjavik city center via private luxury transfer (pre-arranged). Check in early or store luggage at a premium Reykjavik hotel. Rest and freshen up before beginning the journey north to Siglufjörður.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Reykjavik by private chauffeured vehicle heading north along Route 1 and then Route 76 toward Siglufjörður (approx. 4–5 hours). Stop en route at Borgarnes Settlement Center for a brief cultural introduction to Iceland's Viking heritage. Continue through dramatic lava fields and coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður. Check in and settle into your room overlooking the fjord. Take a short stroll along the quiet harbor to absorb the atmosphere of this charming fishing village. Dine at the hotel's own restaurant, which serves locally sourced Icelandic cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments on board the flight or at Keflavík Airport's premium lounge
meals.lunch: Stop at Hótel Bifröst restaurant or a quality roadside café en route for a warm bowl of Icelandic lamb soup
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — fresh Arctic char, slow-braised lamb shank, and skyr-based dessert paired with Icelandic craft beer

day_by_day.notes: Given the very early arrival and long drive north, keep Day 1 relaxed. January daylight in Siglufjörður is extremely limited (roughly 5–6 hours), so the drive will be partly in darkness. Ensure the private transfer is pre-booked. Pack warm layers accessible in carry-on for the cold arrival.

day_by_day.morning: After a restorative night's sleep, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Take a guided walk around Siglufjörður's historic herring-era harbor with a local guide. Visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), one of Iceland's finest regional museums, to learn about the town's fascinating fishing history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or arrange a guided snowshoe or winter hiking excursion into the mountains surrounding Siglufjörður. The Héðinsfjörður valley, accessible via a short tunnel, offers stunning frozen fjord scenery and complete solitude. Return to town and warm up at the local geothermal hot pot (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — a small but authentic community pool with outdoor hot tubs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hotel Siglunes. After dinner, step outside or take a short drive to a dark-sky vantage point above the fjord for a Northern Lights watch. January offers long dark nights and excellent aurora potential in this remote northern location.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — skyr, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs, and fresh coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch prepared by the hotel for the outdoor excursion — thermos of soup, artisan sandwiches, and Icelandic chocolate
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — pan-seared cod with butter sauce, root vegetable purée, and a selection of Icelandic cheeses to finish

day_by_day.notes: Confirm snowshoe or hiking guide availability in advance. The community pool hours may be limited on Sundays — check ahead. Dress in full thermal layers for the evening aurora watch; temperatures can drop to -10°C or below with wind chill.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the hotel. Embark on a private guided whale-watching and sea-bird tour from Siglufjörður harbor (winter tours operate with specialist guides; humpback and minke whales are occasionally spotted). Alternatively, if sea conditions are rough, opt for a private photography tour of the fjord's dramatic winter landscapes with a local photographer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Tröllaskagi peninsula route toward Hofsós and Sauðárkrókur. Stop at Hofsós Infinity Pool — a stunning geothermal pool perched on a cliff edge overlooking Skagafjörður fjord, one of Iceland's most spectacular bathing experiences. Soak for 1–2 hours while gazing across the icy fjord.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður along the coastal road. Enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel with a private in-room dining option or a relaxed dinner in the restaurant. Keep curtains open or set an aurora alert app for potential Northern Lights activity.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes full breakfast buffet
meals.lunch: Light café lunch in Hofsós or Sauðárkrókur — fresh fish soup and Icelandic flatbread
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — slow-roasted reindeer with juniper berry sauce, roasted root vegetables, and Icelandic schnapps digestif

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós pool is approximately 1 hour from Siglufjörður. Bring a swimsuit and towel (rentals available). The drive along the Tröllaskagi peninsula is scenic but can be icy — ensure the vehicle has winter tires. Check road conditions at road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow morning at Hotel Siglunes. Arrange a private guided ice-fishing experience on one of the frozen lakes near Siglufjörður with a local expert. Learn traditional Icelandic ice-fishing techniques and, if successful, have your catch prepared for lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Music Center (Þórbergssetur) to experience traditional Icelandic music and culture. Afterward, explore the town's small artisan shops and galleries. Stop at a local bakery for freshly baked Icelandic pastries and coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Private Northern Lights excursion by 4WD vehicle with a local guide who monitors aurora forecasts in real time. Drive to elevated dark-sky locations above the fjord for optimal viewing. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate and a warm blanket. Photography assistance provided by the guide.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon on rye, fresh juice, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Hotel kitchen prepares your ice-caught fish (if successful) — pan-fried Arctic char with lemon butter and herbs; alternatively, a gourmet packed lunch
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — Icelandic lamb rack with rosemary and garlic, accompanied by a curated Icelandic wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Ice-fishing requires advance booking through the hotel concierge. The evening aurora excursion should be booked with a local guide service — the hotel can arrange this. Aurora activity is weather-dependent; have a backup plan of stargazing or a cozy evening by the fire.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, embark on a full-day private excursion to Akureyri, Iceland's 'Capital of the North' (approximately 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður). Arrive in Akureyri and visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched above the town. Explore the charming pedestrian shopping street, Hafnarstræti.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — even in winter the grounds are atmospheric. Then head to the Geosea Geothermal Sea Baths in nearby Húsavík direction or the Forest Lagoon (Skógarböð) near Akureyri — a premium geothermal spa experience with infinity pools overlooking the fjord and birch forest. Spend 2 hours soaking in the heated mineral-rich waters.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at one of Akureyri's finest restaurants before the scenic drive back to Siglufjörður. Alternatively, stay overnight in Akureyri at a premium hotel if preferred (optional upgrade).

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes full breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Rub23 restaurant in Akureyri — renowned for its sushi and Icelandic seafood fusion in an elegant setting
meals.dinner: Strikið restaurant in Akureyri — panoramic fjord views, premium Icelandic beef tenderloin and fresh langoustine; return to Siglufjörður after dinner

day_by_day.notes: The Forest Lagoon (Skógarböð) is a newer premium spa facility near Akureyri and should be booked well in advance. The drive back to Siglufjörður after dinner will be in full darkness — ensure a reliable driver or private transfer. Road conditions on Route 82 can be challenging in January.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning at Hotel Siglunes. Enjoy a late, indulgent breakfast. Arrange a private guided cross-country skiing or snowmobile tour in the mountains above Siglufjörður — the town is surrounded by dramatic ski terrain and the local ski area (Skarðsdalur) is one of Iceland's best-kept secrets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a warm lunch. Spend the afternoon in a private wellness session — arrange an in-room massage or spa treatment through the hotel concierge. Alternatively, visit the local geothermal pool again for a relaxing soak.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private cultural evening arranged by the hotel — a local musician or storyteller sharing Icelandic sagas and folk tales by firelight. Keep the evening open for spontaneous Northern Lights viewing if the forecast is favorable.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — smoked lamb, pickled herring, fresh pastries, and Icelandic dairy products
meals.lunch: Hotel Siglunes — hearty Icelandic meat soup (kjötsúpa) with freshly baked bread
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — five-course tasting menu featuring seasonal Icelandic ingredients, paired with curated wines

day_by_day.notes: Snowmobile tours require advance booking and a valid driving license. Ski equipment rental is available locally. The five-course tasting menu should be requested from the hotel in advance to allow the kitchen to prepare.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siglufjörður after breakfast for a scenic drive south toward Reykjavik (approximately 5–6 hours with stops). Travel via the Tröllaskagi peninsula and stop at Varmahlíð in Skagafjörður for a visit to the Glaumbær turf farm museum — one of Iceland's best-preserved historic farmsteads.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south, stopping at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls in the Borgarfjörður region — a series of ethereal lava waterfalls that remain partially unfrozen even in winter. Arrive in Reykjavik by late afternoon and check in to a luxury hotel (e.g., The Retreat at Blue Lagoon, Hotel Borg, or ION Adventure Hotel).
day_by_day.evening: Freshen up and enjoy a premium dinner in Reykjavik's vibrant restaurant scene. Explore the illuminated streets of the old town around Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before checkout
meals.lunch: Stop at Hotel Varmahlíð or a quality roadside restaurant in Skagafjörður for Icelandic lamb stew
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant in Reykjavik — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a Nordic tasting menu with locally foraged and seasonal ingredients (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Reykjavik luxury hotel well in advance. Dill Restaurant requires reservations weeks ahead. The drive south covers varied terrain — check road.is for conditions. Consider an overnight stop in Borgarnes if the drive feels too long.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the Laugardalslaug Geothermal Pool — Reykjavik's largest public geothermal pool complex. Arrive early to enjoy the outdoor hot pots, steam rooms, and lap pools before the weekend crowds arrive. Afterward, explore the adjacent Laugardalur park and botanical garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hlemmur Mathöll food hall for a gourmet lunch experience sampling Iceland's best artisan food vendors. Then explore the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) for a deep dive into Icelandic history and culture, followed by a walk to Hallgrímskirkja church and the Harpa Concert Hall.
day_by_day.evening: Join a guided Northern Lights Hunt from Reykjavik — a premium minibus tour with expert aurora guides who monitor forecasts in real time and drive to optimal dark-sky locations outside the city. Tours typically depart around 21:00 and last 3–4 hours.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit Brauð & Co bakery on Frakkastígur for freshly baked Icelandic pastries and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Hlemmur Mathöll food hall — sample langoustine tacos, Icelandic hot dogs (pylsur), artisan cheeses, and craft beer
meals.dinner: Grillið at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel — rooftop fine dining with panoramic Reykjavik views; Icelandic beef and fresh seafood

day_by_day.notes: The Northern Lights Hunt should be booked in advance through a reputable operator. Success depends on clear skies and solar activity — January offers long dark nights which maximize chances. Dress in full winter gear for the evening tour.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Golden Circle Day Tour with a private luxury guide. Begin at Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet and Iceland's ancient parliament (Alþingi) was established. Walk the dramatic Almannagjá canyon in the crisp winter air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir geothermal area to witness Strokkur geyser erupting every 5–10 minutes in dramatic winter steam clouds. Then visit Gullfoss waterfall — Iceland's most iconic cascade, partially frozen in winter and utterly spectacular. Stop at a local greenhouse tomato farm for a unique farm-to-table experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a premium dinner. If aurora forecast is strong, take a short drive outside the city for another viewing opportunity.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast before the early departure
meals.lunch: Friðheimar greenhouse restaurant near Geysir — unique dining inside a working tomato greenhouse; tomato soup, tomato-based dishes, and Bloody Marys (reservation required)
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavik — traditional Icelandic recipes reimagined with modern technique; salt cod, hákarl-inspired dishes, and skyr desserts

day_by_day.notes: Friðheimar requires advance reservation and is one of Iceland's most unique dining experiences. The Golden Circle roads are generally well-maintained but can be icy — a private 4WD vehicle with an experienced driver is recommended. Dress in full winter layers for outdoor stops.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure experience at Þingvellir National Park (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavik). Don a dry suit and snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in some of the world's clearest glacial water (visibility up to 100 meters). A truly once-in-a-lifetime experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik and warm up with a hot lunch. Visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Listasafn Reykjavíkur) or the Icelandic Phallological Museum for a quirky cultural experience. Spend the afternoon exploring the colorful streets of the 101 Reykjavik district and browsing premium Icelandic design shops.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a premium spa evening at one of Reykjavik's luxury hotel spas (e.g., the spa at Canopy by Hilton or the Retreat Spa). Follow with a fine dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before the Silfra excursion — the dry suit fitting requires an empty stomach
meals.lunch: Kopar restaurant at the Old Harbour — fresh Icelandic seafood with harbour views; langoustine, scallops, and Arctic char
meals.dinner: Ox restaurant (below Grillið) — intimate underground fine dining, one of Reykjavik's most exclusive tables; tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling requires advance booking and a medical fitness declaration. Minimum water temperature is approximately 2–4°C — dry suits are provided but fingers and face will be cold. Not suitable for non-swimmers. Minimum age and health requirements apply. Book weeks in advance as spots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — book the premium Retreat Spa package for the ultimate luxury experience. Arrive at opening time to enjoy the milky-blue silica-rich waters, in-water bar service, silica mud masks, and algae masks. The Retreat at Blue Lagoon offers a private lagoon section for an even more exclusive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at the Blue Lagoon complex. Enjoy the steam caves, sauna, and relaxation lounges. Have lunch at the Lava Restaurant inside the Blue Lagoon complex, which offers gourmet Icelandic cuisine with views directly over the geothermal waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik by private transfer. Spend the evening exploring Reykjavik's nightlife on Laugavegur street, or enjoy a quiet premium cocktail bar experience at Slippbarinn at Icelandair Hotel Reykjavik Marina.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure to Blue Lagoon
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — Icelandic seafood platter, langoustine bisque, and freshly baked sourdough; book a table in advance
meals.dinner: Fiskfélagið (Fish Company) in Reykjavik — creative Icelandic seafood in a historic cellar setting; tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Lagoon Retreat package must be booked well in advance — it sells out months ahead. Bring or purchase a high-quality hair conditioner as the silica water can be drying. The Retreat package includes towels, robes, and slippers. Arrive early to maximize time before afternoon crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private day tour to the South Coast of Iceland. Depart Reykjavik and drive along the Ring Road to Seljalandsfoss waterfall — in winter, the falls are dramatically framed by ice formations. Walk behind the curtain of water (if conditions permit). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall, equally spectacular with winter ice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — one of the world's most dramatic beaches, with towering basalt columns, sea stacks, and powerful Atlantic waves. Explore the nearby Dyrhólaey promontory for panoramic coastal views. Stop at the Katla Geopark visitor center to learn about Iceland's volcanic geology.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik as darkness falls. Enjoy a final premium dinner in the city. If the aurora forecast is favorable, arrange one last Northern Lights excursion or simply watch from a dark spot outside the city.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before the early departure
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch from the hotel or stop at Skógar Guesthouse café near Skógafoss for hot soup and coffee
meals.dinner: Geysir Bistro & Bar or Apotek Kitchen & Bar in central Reykjavik — modern Icelandic cuisine in an elegant setting; Icelandic lamb, fresh fish, and premium desserts

day_by_day.notes: Exercise extreme caution at Reynisfjara beach — sneaker waves are a serious hazard year-round. Never turn your back on the ocean. The walk behind Seljalandsfoss may be icy and closed in severe winter conditions — check locally. The South Coast drive is approximately 3–4 hours round trip from Reykjavik.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the hotel. Pack and check out. Depending on departure time, visit the Reykjavik Flea Market (Kolaportið) at the harbour for last-minute Icelandic souvenirs, or browse premium design stores on Skólavörðustígur for Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), ceramics, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavik). Arrive at the airport with ample time for check-in and security. Relax in the airport's premium lounge before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with extraordinary memories of the Northern Lights, geothermal wonders, dramatic winter landscapes, and the unique magic of the Arctic north.

meals.breakfast: Final indulgent hotel breakfast — smoked salmon, Icelandic skyr with berries, fresh pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Keflavík Airport premium lounge or a farewell meal at a Reykjavik restaurant near the hotel before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or upon arrival at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for the airport transfer and check-in process. Purchase any duty-free Icelandic spirits (Brennivín schnapps) or Icelandic chocolates at the airport. Confirm the private transfer booking the evening before. Consider purchasing travel insurance that covers weather-related disruptions, which are common in Iceland in January.
